Hi Anna / Michael —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and lots of alignment on the use case. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key asks and next steps so we can get you a concise economics model and a formal quote.

- A clear $/1M tokens target and how that maps to your budget range
- Estimated token volumes by feature (chat, summaries, enrichment) and expected monthly totals
- Unit economics per feature (inference cost, expected margin after Redwood fees)

What I need from you (quick confirm):
1) Expected monthly MAUs for the pilot and full roll-out (ballpark is fine)
2) Average tokens per interaction by feature (chat conv length, summary length, enrichment calls)
3) Target monthly budget range for inference (e.g., $10k-$50k/month) or a target $/1M tokens you want us to hit

Attachments: I’ve attached a simple mutual-action plan (FintechX_MA_plan.xlsx) with suggested milestones and a proposed timeline for pilot -> prod.

Next steps (proposed):
- Anna: reply with the three items above (or let us know if we should assume defaults) — by Mon 03/02
- Redwood: Dev and Rishi will prepare a unit-economics deep-dive and pricing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) — deliver by Wed 03/04
- Align on a short scoping call if needed to clarify token assumptions

If you prefer, I can draft a few $/1M scenarios now and we’ll refine once we get your numbers.

Thanks Marissa — great to meet you and the team. Quick answers below (high level) so you can start modeling:

1) Pilot / rollout volumes
- Pilot (3 months): ~10k MAU active users, expected ~25k weekly active users in app over time for full rollout
- Target production: 100k MAU in 12 months (rough roadmap)

2) Tokens per feature (averages)
- Chat (primary): ~400 tokens per session (multi-turn), ~2 sessions per MAU / week initially
- Summaries (batch): ~1,500 tokens per summary, ~0.2 summaries per MAU / week
- Enrichment (API calls): ~150 tokens per call, ~3 calls per MAU / week

This maps roughly to: pilot ~120M tokens/month; prod ~1.2B tokens/month (order of magnitude).

3) Budget target / $/1M tokens
- Pilot budget: $10k-$25k/month (flexible)
- We are targeting an effective unit cost of ~$300 / 1M tokens (to make the feature economics work for our pricing model). If Redwood can show scenarios at $200, $300, and $400 / 1M tokens that’d be ideal.

Procurement is looped for early visibility. If you need any historic traffic data or product logs to refine token estimates, let me know.

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Unit-economics deep-dive (FintechX numbers)

Marissa / Rishi —

Attached is a concise model I put together; below are the key outputs and assumptions (high level) so we can share with Anna / procurement. Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf) and quick math inline.

Assumptions from FintechX: pilot = 120M tokens/month; prod = 1.2B tokens/month. Token mix: chat 65%, summaries 10%, enrichment 25%.

Redwood indicative $/1M-token (hosted vs dedicated vs private) — ballpark, pre-negotiation:
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go, multi-tenant, standard model): $420 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, 30-day commit, optimized quantization): $250 / 1M tokens
- Private (on-prem / VPC with license + infra): equivalent infra + license -> effective $180 - $220 / 1M tokens (depends on infra amortization)

Per-feature cost (pilot, 120M tokens):
- Chat (65% = 78M tokens): Hosted = $32,760/mo; Dedicated = $19,500/mo; Private = $14,040 - $17,160/mo
- Summaries (10% = 12M tokens): Hosted = $5,040/mo; Dedicated = $3,000/mo; Private = $2,160 - $2,640/mo
- Enrichment (25% = 30M tokens): Hosted = $12,600/mo; Dedicated = $7,500/mo; Private = $5,400 - $6,600/mo

Total monthly inference cost (pilot): Hosted ~$50,400/mo; Dedicated ~$30,000/mo; Private ~$21,600 - $26,400/mo

$/feature per MAU (pilot, 10k MAU):
- Chat cost / MAU = Hosted $3.276 / MAU / mo; Dedicated $1.95; Private $1.404 - $1.716
- Summaries / MAU = Hosted $0.504; Dedicated $0.300; Private $0.216 - $0.264
- Enrichment / MAU = Hosted $1.26; Dedicated $0.75; Private $0.54 - $0.66
- Total cost / MAU / mo (pilot): Hosted ~$5.04; Dedicated ~$3.00; Private ~$2.16 - $2.64

CAC payback (example scenarios):
- If CAC = $1,500 and ARPU = $30/mo -> payback
  - Hosted: 1,500 / (30 - 5.04) ≈ 63 months (not viable)
  - Dedicated: 1,500 / (30 - 3.00) ≈ 58 months
  - Private: 1,500 / (30 - 2.64) ≈ 55 months

- If CAC = $3,000 and ARPU = $50/mo -> payback
  - Hosted: 3,000 / (50 - 5.04) ≈ 68 months
  - Dedicated: 3,000 / (50 - 3.00) ≈ 66 months
  - Private: 3,000 / (50 - 2.64) ≈ 64 months

Notes / commentary:
- The current ARPU assumptions are too low given the token intensity. To reach healthy payback (<12 months) we either need: higher ARPU (>$200/mo), materially lower CAC (<$500), or lower effective $/1M tokens (private infra + tight quantization + caching) closer to $50-$100 / 1M.
- Opportunities to improve economics: aggressive prefix/KV caching for common prompts, model quantization to reduce GPU cost, batching policies and routing lower-priority traffic to cheaper capacity.
- We should propose a 60-90 day pilot on Dedicated with conservative commit (e.g., 3-6 month discount) to demonstrate cost per 1M at scale and capture real token distributions.

I’ll tidy the attached model and create a one-page comparison table for Anna. Thoughts before I share externally?

— Dev
